Title: Stored XSS via unescaped job.display_class in multiple Web UI views
Analysis:
### Source:
Untrusted user input enters through job payloads enqueued via `Sidekiq::Client.push` (e.g. from an API endpoint, user-facing feature, or client process) where an attacker specifies a custom `'class'` or `'display_class'` value such as `"<script>alert('xss')</script>"`.

### Sanitization/Validation:
No sanitization, validation, or escaping is performed on the class name when enqueuing the job or when retrieval of the job payload occurs.

### Sink:
When the administrator views the job details page or various queues on the Web UI, the unescaped value is rendered directly via `<%= job.display_class %>` or `<%= entry.display_class %>` in multiple views:
- `/web/views/_job_info.erb` (line 17)
- `/web/views/busy.erb` (line 138)
- `/web/views/morgue.erb` (line 42)
- `/web/views/retries.erb` (line 44)
- `/web/views/scheduled.erb` (line 41)

This allows an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the Sidekiq Web UI administrator's session.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload:
Enqueue a job with a malicious class payload:
```ruby
Sidekiq::Client.push(
  'class' => '<script>alert("XSS")</script>',
  'args' => []
)
```
When an administrator views the retries, scheduled, busy, or morgue page, or visits the job's individual status page, the payload is executed.

Title: Stored XSS via unescaped job class names in Web UI Metrics page (CVE-2024-32887)
Analysis:
### Source:
Untrusted user input enters through job payloads enqueued via `Sidekiq::Client.push` (e.g. from an API endpoint or client process) where an attacker specifies a custom `'class'` or `'wrapped'` value such as `"</canvas><script>alert('xss')</script>"`.

### Sanitization/Validation:
No sanitization, validation, or escaping is performed on the class name when recording execution metrics. Metrics are stored in Redis as keys of the format `"j|YYYYMMDD|HH:MM"`, containing fields of the form `"class_name|metric"`.

### Sink:
When the administrator views the Metrics page (`/metrics`), the Web UI retrieves the job metrics and parses the class name from the keys. The raw unescaped class name is rendered directly into the HTML page in multiple places:
1. Inside the `<canvas>` element via `to_json` serialization (which does not escape HTML characters like `<` or `>` by default), allowing attackers to close the canvas and inject script tags (line 39).
2. Inside the metrics table checklist and link labels via `<%= kls %>` (lines 70 and 73).

This allows an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the Sidekiq Web UI administrator's session.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload:
Enqueue a job with a malicious class payload:
```ruby
Sidekiq::Client.push(
  'class' => '</canvas><script>alert("XSS")</script>',
  'args' => []
)
```
When this job finishes executing (or fails), its execution metrics are logged. Once an administrator visits `/metrics`, the script is executed.
